name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, including about 1,800 in DR Congo, mostly in the conflict-hit east
state: WHO says DR Congo has recorded more than 60,000 cholera cases and about 1,800 deaths in 2026, and cases reported in Kingabwa in eastern Kinshasa in early November raised fears of spread to the capital (DW via AllAfrica, 6 Nov). WHO said on 11 Nov that more than 3,000 people have died of cholera worldwide in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa (Ahram Online, citing AFP). ECDC's 27 Oct update lists the largest recent outbreaks in Nigeria, DR Congo and South Sudan. Searches on 28 Nov found no sign these outbreaks are ending, so the Alert holds.
for_you: People in eastern DR Congo, South Sudan, Nigeria and Yemen are most exposed. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice and NHS fit-for-travel guidance on safe water and cholera vaccination.
rubric_hit: Alert: large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (DR Congo ~1,800 deaths in 2026, WHO)

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
